newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus security lapses blamed in Israelis' trial.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus security lapses blamed in Israelis' trial.

text.p: Defence lawyers for three Israelis charged with escaping police custody appealed for leniency at a Cyprus court on Monday saying lax police security tempted the defendants.
On Wednesday the three-bench Cypriot criminal court will pass sentences on defendants David Biton, 24, Amon Shimon, 28, and Shuki Samana, 24.

"The accused had a happy-go-lucky approach," said Phoivos Clerides, the lawyer for Biton and Shimon. "They acted without coordination and these incidents emanated from police neglect in preventing a crime," he said.
The first two are charged with aiding the escape of Samana and a fourth man, Biton's brother Avi, 21, by holding up a police car on a busy street in central Nicosia in mid-September.

Samana and Avi Biton were in custody at the time on suspicion of distributing forged $100 bills. Police were taking the two from the island's central prisons in capital Nicosia to the coastal town of Larnaca when the unescorted vehicle was intercepted.
All three have pleaded guilty to the charges, which carry prison sentences of two years and upwards.
Clerides urged the three-bench court to exercise the "utmost leniency" in passing sentence.

David Biton and Shimon got the other two suspects out of the police car, left stranded at traffic lights, put them on the back of their high-powered motorcycles and roared through a United Nations checkpoint close by leading to Turkish-held northern Cyprus.

But the defendants would not have been able to threaten the police officers with a pistol and a knife and cut the police two-way radio if one of the officers hadn't rolled down the car window, Clerides said.
Turkish Cypriot police officers returned the four the same day.
Avi Shimon did not appear before the court, which last month jailed him for two-and-a-half years on charges of possession and distribution of 72 forged $100 bills in August.
His appearance before the court was rendered unnecessary because the earlier verdict took into account charges emanating from the escape attempt.
